sources: MONDAY Sep 28 2026 RUN (06:30 UTC). Asia is trading and US cash is shut, so this is a live-commodity/FX read with US cash prints carried from the Friday Sep 25 close. THE MOVE: Brent 107.64 USD/Bbl (TradingEconomics, Sep 28, +3.18 pct on the day; the same page shows 107.858 / +3.39 pct intraday), up from 104.32 at the Friday close. Trump REJECTED Iran's proposal for a phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend, and Iran said it will not soften its demands, so the de-escalation headline that knocked 2.1 pct off Brent on Friday has fully reversed. Brent is now roughly +24 pct on the month. Sources: CNBC Sep 28 (Brent +2.7 pct on the Trump rejection), Bloomberg Sep 28 (Iran won't soften Hormuz demands), Outlook India, Invezz, CBS News live updates (Trump expects talks to resume this week). GOLD BREAKDOWN - copper/gold 1.58, up from 1.56. Copper 6.60 USD/Lbs (TradingEconomics Sep 28, -1.45 pct) and gold 4,174.37 USD/t.oz (TradingEconomics Sep 28, -2.58 pct); 6.60/4174.37*1000 = 1.581. Note the ratio is rising for the WRONG reason: copper is falling too, gold is just falling faster. Gold broke below 4,200 (NordFX Market Pulse Sep 28 had it at 4,197, Yahoo's Sunday-evening snapshot 4,231.30) on 5 pct-plus long-end yields and Fed hike pricing, not on any growth improvement. Trend up, but this is a real-rate shock, not a cyclical signal. CURVE CONFIRMED AND STEEPER: 2s10s 0.36 (FRED T10Y2Y, Sep 25). The full week is 0.20 (Sep 21), 0.25, 0.26, 0.31, 0.36 - five straight sessions of bear steepening, +16bp on the week. HIGH confidence, primary print. Long end: 10y 5.20 pct and 30y 5.513 pct as of Sunday evening ET (Yahoo Finance snapshot), 30y a two-decade high and up about 27bp on the month (NordFX Sep 28). Five- and ten-year yields are at their highest since 2007 (Briefs.co). RATES VOL: MOVE carried at 104.58, still the Sep 24 close (Saxo Bank Options Brief Sep 25: +9.56 pct that session, +33 pct over two sessions, above all 60 prior three-month readings). No Sep 25 or Sep 28 print retrievable; MacroMicro is gated. Corroborating weekly magnitude: KuCoin flash Sep 28 has MOVE +19 pct on the week and Briefs.co has about +29.7 pct, the largest weekly jump since April 2025 and levels last seen in March after the Iran war began. Trend up, MEDIUM confidence on the level. EQUITY VOL STILL ASLEEP: VIX 14.87, the Sep 25 close (-5.11 pct). Against 14.87 on Sep 21 that is exactly FLAT week-over-week. S&P futures -0.33 pct, Nasdaq-100 -0.60 pct, Dow -0.30 pct Sunday evening; KOSPI -2.4 pct and Shanghai -1.4 pct in Asia. The MOVE-versus-VIX divergence is the defining feature of this episode and it is still widening. CREDIT: HY OAS 280bp (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2, 2.80 pct dated Sep 24 - today's scheduled print had not landed as of this run). Week: 268 (Sep 18), 266, 268, 273, 280. Trend up. This remains the one credit signal that has genuinely repriced; 300 is the level to watch. BREAKEVENS STILL NOT CONFIRMING: 5y5y forward inflation 2.34 pct (FRED T5YIFR, Sep 25) versus 2.35 on Sep 21 - flat, and flat through a week in which Brent went up 3 pct and the 30y made a two-decade high. The long-end selloff is a real-rate and term-premium story, not an inflation-expectations story. That is the single most important thing on this dashboard. DXY 101.08 (TradingEconomics, Sep 27/28, +0.11 pct), dollar firming with EUR/USD 1.1386 just under Friday's close. Trend up. NFCI -0.56 for the week ending Sep 18 (Chicago Fed via FRED), still the loosest of the cycle, flat; next print Sep 30. Global liquidity 1 (stable). CARRIED, no new releases: initial claims 197k (week ending Sep 19, DOL, next Oct 1), ISM manufacturing 54.6 (August, next Oct 1), UMich consumer sentiment 48.1 (final September, a four-month low, -7.0 pct from 51.7 in August), building permits 1,403k (August, -2.1 pct m/m, trend down, next Oct 17), LEI y/y about -0.7 pct (August), Sahm rule -0.07 (August, next Oct 2), SOFR-OIS 0bp and EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis -10bp (standing assumptions, no free live source). BDTI DATA FLAG - EIGHTH consecutive run carried at 4,899. Still no dated Baltic print: Investing.com stale at 1,107 dated 31/03, StockQ rows empty, MacroMicro gated, Baltic Exchange subscription-only. New context found this run: the Baltic Exchange has been running a consultation since April 2026 on amending or suspending its Middle East Gulf tanker benchmarks because of Hormuz security risk, and Circular 44/26 (Jul 21, feedback closed Aug 3) proposes allowing load ports outside the Gulf into the BDTI, BCTI and BLPG assessments (Xinde Marine News). So the BDTI itself is under methodology reform precisely because of the shock this dashboard is trying to measure - which means the field is not merely a broken scrape, it may be a benchmark in transition. LOW confidence; treat as non-informative and either wire a paid source or drop it. PICTURE: the Hormuz de-escalation was a one-day headline and it is gone. Oil is back above the Friday spike, the long end is at multi-decade highs, and the market is pricing more Fed hikes into an economy whose domestic data is soft (UMich 48.1, LEI negative y/y, permits falling) but whose labor market has not cracked (claims 197k). That is textbook policy-error geometry. The stress is concentrated in rates vol (MOVE about +20 to 30 pct on the week) and has begun to leak into credit (HY OAS 268 to 280). The three holdouts are equity vol (VIX flat at 14.87), NFCI at the loosest of the cycle, and breakevens at 2.34. Gold falling 2.6 pct alongside copper while oil rips is a liquidation signature, not a rotation. WATCH: HY OAS through 300 (FRED print due today), whether MOVE holds above 100 and whether VIX finally converges once US cash opens, whether the 10y breaks 5.25, NFCI Sep 30, ISM manufacturing and initial claims Oct 1, Sahm rule Oct 2, and any concrete Iran talks this week.
